stories.title: Somalia Chairs EAC Speakers' Bureau Meeting in Arusha, Secures Hosting Rights for 2027 Summit
stories.description: ARUSHA — The Speaker of Somalia’s House of the People, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur (Jama), chaired the 21st meeting of the Bureau of Speakers of East African Community (EAC) parliaments in Arusha, Tanzania, on Friday, consolidating Somalia’s parliamentary engagement with the regional bloc it joined in 2024. The meeting focused on strengthening parliamentary cooperation, advancing parliamentary diplomacy, exchanging expertise, and ensuring that East African integration delivers tangible benefits to the people of the region. Speaker Jama briefed his counterparts on the progress of Somalia’s 11th Federal Parliament, highlighting achievements in state-building, the completion and ratification of the provisional constitution, security and the rule of law, public financial management, and economic development. He noted that the House of the People has approved more than 56 laws and 18 resolutions. He emphasised that the House’s goal is to fully discharge its constitutional responsibilities, particularly legislation and oversight, to serve the interests of the Somali people and contribute to strengthening cooperation and integration within the East African Community. Somalia to Host 22nd EAC Speakers’ Bureau Meeting Speaker Jama announced that Somalia is ready to host the 22nd meeting of the Bureau of Speakers of EAC parliaments in Mogadishu at the end of January 2027. He expressed optimism that Mogadishu would welcome the Bureau and that the meeting would reinforce joint efforts toward building a united, prosperous East African Community living in lasting peace. He stressed that the future of the East African Community depends on strong cooperation, resilient institutions and parliaments that work effectively for the interests and aspirations of their peoples, and that Somalia is committed to playing its full role in achieving that vision. stories.title: The impact of nocturnal hypokinesia on supervised and unsupervised mobility in people with Parkinson’s disease
stories.description: Nocturnal hypokinesia (NH) is a disabling and underrecognized symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), affecting nighttime movements and sleep quality. However, its impact on daytime mobility remains unclear. This study investigated supervised and unsupervised mobility in propensity score-matched mild-to-moderate PD patients with (PD NH + ) and without NH (PD NH − ). Eighty-eight participants (44 PD NH+ and 44 PD NH-) underwent clinical assessments, mobility tests (i.e., 20-m forward walking, instrumented Timed-Up-and-Go and 3-metre backward walking test), and 5-day monitoring of average daily steps (AvDS) through a commercial activity tracker (Garmin Vivosmart 4). PD NH+ demonstrated worse functional mobility, reduced turning velocity, slower backwards walking, and fewer AvDS than PD NH-. Furthermore, NH severity correlated negatively with most supervised measures and with AvDS. However, sensitivity analyses controlling for fear of falling attenuated group differences in supervised mobility to non-significance, suggesting a preliminary nature of these findings. The association between NH severity and daily step count showed greater robustness. These findings suggest that NH could be associated with impaired daytime mobility and worse motor function. These findings highlight the importance of targeted interventions to address both nocturnal and diurnal mobility impairments in PD.

stories.title: Altered miR-30c and miR-127 expression and NF-κB/NLRP3-related transcriptional changes are associated with metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation in adult males with sleep deprivation and habitual c
stories.description: Chronic sleep deprivation and habitual coffee consumption are common overlapping behaviours, yet the post-transcriptional expression patterns associated with their metabolic and inflammatory correlates remain poorly defined. This study examined alterations in the regulatory microRNAs miR-30c and miR-127 and transcript-level expression changes consistent with involvement of the NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory axis, together with their metabolic and inflammatory correlates, in adult males. Two hundred male volunteers aged 30–50 years were classified into four groups of 50 according to sleep pattern and coffee intake: healthy controls (HC; normal sleep, no habitual coffee consumption), habitual coffee consumers (CF), sleep-deprived subjects (SD), and a combined sleep-deprived, coffee-consuming group (SD + CF). Expression of miR-30c, miR-127, NLRP3, and NF-κB p65 (RELA) was assessed by quantitative real-time PCR. Fasting glucose was measured by the glucose oxidase method, the lipid profile by enzymatic colorimetry, and serum IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-10 by ELISA. Compared with healthy controls, the SD + CF group showed marked downregulation of miR-30c and miR-127 and pronounced upregulation of NLRP3 mRNA (all p < 0.001), accompanied by increased NF-κB p65 expression (3.79-fold; p < 0.001). These molecular changes were paralleled by significantly elevated IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α and reduced IL-10, as well as higher fasting glucose (108.5 ± 12.3 vs. 89.2 ± 8.6 mg/dL; p < 0.001), total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, and triglycerides, with reduced HDL-cholesterol (all p < 0.05). In pairwise comparisons, the CF group differed significantly from HC only in fasting glucose, whereas the combined SD + CF group showed the most pronounced metabolic, inflammatory, and molecular alterations. Two-way factorial analysis identified significant Sleep × Coffee interactions for LDL-cholesterol, triglycerides, IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, NF-κB p65, miR-30c, miR-127, and NLRP3. Chronic sleep deprivation, particularly when accompanied by habitual coffee consumption, is associated with altered miR-30c and miR-127 expression and an expression pattern consistent with involvement of the NF-κB/NLRP3 axis, alongside metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation in adult males, with statistical evidence of a combined, potentiating association between the two exposures for several inflammatory and molecular outcomes. These findings add a post-transcriptional dimension to the understanding of how insufficient sleep and habitual coffee consumption relate to cardiometabolic risk.

stories.title: Ultra-dispersed metal oxide nanoparticles on graphitic carbon nitride as functional platforms for electrochemical nitrate valorization
stories.description: Ammonia is a vital commodity of key importance for global agriculture, but its traditional synthesis via the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process features a high ecological footprint, contributing to ≈2% of the overall carbon dioxide emission. An eco-friendly and sustainable alternative is offered by electrochemical NO3− reduction (e-NO3RR), enabling also to simultaneously reduce the concentration of nitrate, a widespread water pollutant. Herein, we report on the ultra-dispersion of CuFe2O4, NiFe2O4, or Fe2O3 nanoparticles (NPs) on graphitic carbon nitride (gCN), yielding heterostructured oxide@gCN systems as potential e-NO3RR catalysts. The target materials, fabricated by gCN electrophoretic deposition on carbon cloth (CC), followed by radio frequency (RF)-sputtering of oxide NPs in very low amounts, were subjected to a multi-technique characterization aimed at investigating their morphological, structural, compositional, and optoelectronic properties. The results indicate that gCN provides a robust, electronically coupled scaffold anchoring ultra-dispersed oxides, and evidence a gCN → oxide electron donation. Electrochemical tests coupled with ion chromatographic analyses highlight CuFe2O4@gCN as the best-performing catalyst, affording a Faradaic efficiency towards NH4+ of 21% at -1.15 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), together with a comparatively higher ammonium production rate and reduced NO2− generation. Altogether, our results may pave the way to the potential implementation of functional catalysts for ammonia generation from nitrate‑containing aqueous media.
